LESSON: 'Pinned SHA moved' and 'pinned SHA reaches the built artifact' are different questions and only the second one matters for a bake. In hauska-factory the publish image's LDT content is NOT the LDT checkout: Dockerfile.publish's final stage copies only /ldt/node_modules and /app/bakes, and /app/bakes is an esbuild bundle of the four entrypoints in scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs. Any claim of the form 'commit X changes the bake' is answerable by tracing the transitive import graph of those four, and at 3885efad that graph is 26 modules. This is cheap to run and it overturned the stated urgency of a dispatch.

A `--args=` string in a cloudbuild file proves nothing on its own -- two configs in this repo document `gcloud run jobs execute ... --args=<id>` forms in COMMENTS. Any instrument reading deploy intent out of YAML must strip comment lines and anchor to a `gcloud run jobs deploy` block, and must carry a paired positive test so 'the comment did not match' cannot silently mean 'the parser is broken'.

In hauska-factory an allowlist id is a WRITER identity, not a CLI command (containment-persist is the JOB_ID of p2-juris.mjs, dispatched as p2-juris; p3-rail-absence is p3-absence.mjs). Any control keyed on the allowlist must go through the JOB_ID module, which writer-cli-reachability.test.mjs already learned the hard way after its first predicate fired on four healthy jobs.

A quarantine and an exemption are different artifacts and conflating them launders defects. Six writers here have no deployable target and every one is cloud-gated on --apply, so none is exemptible: they are open defects pinned so the set cannot grow. The test file has to SAY that, or the next reader treats the list as a dispensation.

Bash translates /p/ to P:\ but Node does not, so every `git show` failed silently and the trace reported 4 modules reached with 0 imports -- a confident, wrong, all-green answer. Use 'P:/legacy-design-tools'. The tell was modulesReached exactly equal to the entrypoint count.
